        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Weight the utilities by spatial importance
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_importance
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Set similarity thresholds for strategy selection based on empirical results
    low_similarity_threshold = 0.25  
    high_similarity_threshold = 0.55  
    
    # Generate offspring
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Based on the similarity of parents, choose crossover strategy
        if avg_similarity < low_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are dissimilar - use uniform crossover for exploration
            # Use position utilities to bias inheritance toward higher utility positions
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5
            child = np.where(mask, parent1, parent2)
            
            # Apply utility-based bias: with some probability, swap to the parent with higher utility at that position
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With some probability, pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
                        
        elif avg_similarity > high_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are similar - use multi-point crossover to preserve good building blocks
            # Multi-point crossover with possibility of utility-based adjustments
            num_crossovers = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3], p=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2])  # Updated probabilities
            crossover_points = sorted(np.random.choice(range(1, n_decap), num_crossovers, replace=False))
            
            child = parent1.copy()
            current_parent = 0  # 0 for parent1, 1 for parent2
            
            prev_point = 0
            for cp in crossover_points:
                if current_parent == 0:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent1[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 1
                else:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent2[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 0
                prev_point = cp
            
            # Fill remaining positions with the current parent
            if current_parent == 0:
                child[prev_point:] = parent1[prev_point:]
            else:
                child[prev_point:] = parent2[prev_point:]
                
            # Apply utility-based adjustments to the offspring
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        else:  # Default case: balanced approach with single-point crossover
            # Single-point crossover with utility-guided adjustments
            crossover_point = np.random.randint(1, n_decap)
            child = np.concatenate([parent1[:crossover_point], parent2[crossover_point:]])
            
            # Apply utility-based adjustments
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.2:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements an adaptive crossover operator that selects strategy based on parent similarity.
    Uses Jaccard similarity to measure parent diversity and applies different crossover strategies:
    - Low similarity: Uniform crossover with utility bias for exploration
    - High similarity: Multi-point crossover to preserve building blocks
    - Medium similarity: Single-point crossover with utility guidance
    
    Enhanced utility calculation considers both individual position occurrences and position interactions
    to better capture electrical significance for decap placement.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Analyze parent population characteristics
    # Compute average pairwise similarity across all parent pairs using Jaccard similarity
    similarities = []
    for i in range(n_parents):
        for j in range(i + 1, n_parents):
            if len(set(parents[i]) | set(parents[j])) > 0:  # Avoid division by zero
                jaccard_sim = len(set(parents[i]) & set(parents[j])) / len(set(parents[i]) | set(parents[j]))
                similarities.append(jaccard_sim)
    
    avg_similarity = np.mean(similarities) if similarities else 0.0
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence, spatial factors, and position interactions
    # Consider both how often a position appears and its electrical significance
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Calculate position interaction scores to capture electrical coupling effects
    # Positions that appear together frequently in parents may have synergistic effects
    interaction_scores = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    for parent in parents:
        parent_list = list(parent)
        for i in range(len(parent_list)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(parent_list)):
                pos1, pos2 = parent_list[i], parent_list[j]
                # Add interaction score based on distance - closer positions may interact more
                row1, col1 = pos_to_coords[pos1]
                row2, col2 = pos_to_coords[pos2]
                dist = abs(row1 - row2) + abs(col1 - col2)  # Manhattan distance
                if dist > 0:  # Avoid self-interaction
                    # Add contribution to both positions based on inverse distance
                    interaction_scores[pos1] += 1.0 / dist
                    interaction_scores[pos2] += 1.0 / dist
    
    # Normalize interaction scores
    if interaction_scores.sum() > 0:
        interaction_scores = interaction_scores / interaction_scores.sum()
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    # Positions near center and away from edges may be more electrically significant
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        elif (row in [0, grid_size-1] or col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Edge but not corner
            corner_penalty = 0.9
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance and interaction scores
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Weight the utilities by spatial importance and interaction scores
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_importance * (1 + interaction_scores)
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Set similarity thresholds for strategy selection based on empirical results
    low_similarity_threshold = 0.25  
    high_similarity_threshold = 0.55  
    
    # Generate offspring
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Based on the similarity of parents, choose crossover strategy
        if avg_similarity < low_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are dissimilar - use uniform crossover for exploration
            # Use position utilities to bias inheritance toward higher utility positions
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5
            child = np.where(mask, parent1, parent2)
            
            # Apply utility-based bias: with some probability, swap to the parent with higher utility at that position
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With some probability, pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
                        
        elif avg_similarity > high_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are similar - use multi-point crossover to preserve good building blocks
            # Multi-point crossover with possibility of utility-based adjustments
            num_crossovers = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3], p=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2])  # Updated probabilities
            crossover_points = sorted(np.random.choice(range(1, n_decap), num_crossovers, replace=False))
            
            child = parent1.copy()
            current_parent = 0  # 0 for parent1, 1 for parent2
            
            prev_point = 0
            for cp in crossover_points:
                if current_parent == 0:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent1[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 1
                else:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent2[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 0
                prev_point = cp
            
            # Fill remaining positions with the current parent
            if current_parent == 0:
                child[prev_point:] = parent1[prev_point:]
            else:
                child[prev_point:] = parent2[prev_point:]
                
            # Apply utility-based adjustments to the offspring
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        else:  # Default case: balanced approach with single-point crossover
            # Single-point crossover with utility-guided adjustments
            crossover_point = np.random.randint(1, n_decap)
            child = np.concatenate([parent1[:crossover_point], parent2[crossover_point:]])
            
            # Apply utility-based adjustments
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.2:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize

    # Calculate electrical proxy features
    # Since we don't know the probe location in this function, we calculate generic features

    # Inverse distance to center (electrically significant areas might be near center)
    electrical_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        # Inverse distance to center - higher importance near center
        electrical_importance[pos] = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)
    
    # Local connectivity entropy - measure of how well-connected a position is to its neighbors
    connectivity_entropy = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        
        # Count accessible neighbors (could represent connectivity to power grid)
        neighbors = []
        for dr, dc in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]:  # 4-directional
            nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
            if 0 <= nr < grid_size and 0 <= nc < grid_size:
                neighbors.append(nr * grid_size + nc)

        connectivity_entropy[pos] = len(neighbors) / 4.0  # Normalize to [0, 1]

                        if len(available_for_padding) >= padding_needed:
                            padding_positions = np.random.choice(available_for_padding, size=padding_needed, replace=False)
                        else:
                            # Fallback to allow replacement if not enough unique positions
                            padding_positions = np.random.choice(list(all_positions), size=padding_needed, replace=True)
                        selected_positions.extend(padding_positions)
                
                # Assign the selected positions to the child
                for idx, pos in enumerate(selected_positions):
                    child[n_common_to_use + idx] = pos
                  
            elif avg_similarity > high_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are similar - blend positions with utility bias
                # Use a set-based approach but favor positions with higher utility
                child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
                used_positions = set()
                
                # Get all positions from both parents
                all_parent_positions = list(parent1) + list(parent2)
                position_freq = Counter(all_parent_positions)
                
                # Sort positions by frequency and utility, preferring those that appear in both parents
                position_scores = []
                for pos in set(all_parent_positions):
                    freq_score = position_freq[pos]  # How many times it appears across parents
                    utility_score = position_utilities[pos]
                    # Prefer positions that appear in both parents, then by utility
                    combined_score = freq_score * 10 + utility_score
                    position_scores.append((combined_score, pos))
                
                position_scores.sort(reverse=True)
                ranked_positions = [pos for _, pos in position_scores]
                
                # Fill child with highest-ranked positions first
                n_to_fill = min(n_decap, len(ranked_positions))
                for idx in range(n_to_fill):
                    child[idx] = ranked_positions[idx]
                    used_positions.add(ranked_positions[idx])
                
                # Fill remaining positions from available positions
                if n_to_fill < n_decap:
                    all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                    available_positions = list(all_positions - used_positions)
                    remaining_needed = n_decap - n_to_fill
                    
                    if len(available_positions) >= remaining_needed:
                        # Select based on utility
                        avail_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_positions]
                        avail_sum = sum(avail_utilities)
                        if avail_sum > 0:
                            avail_probs = [u / avail_sum for u in avail_utilities]
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False, p=avail_probs)
                        else:
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        # Not enough unique positions, pad with random
                        extra_positions = available_positions[:]
                        padding_needed = remaining_needed - len(extra_positions)
                        all_remaining = list(set(range(grid_size * grid_size)) - set(extra_positions) - used_positions)
                        if len(all_remaining) >= padding_needed:
                            padding_positions = np.random.choice(all_remaining, size=padding_needed, replace=False)
                        else:
                            padding_positions = np.random.choice(range(grid_size * grid_size), size=padding_needed, replace=True)
                        extra_positions.extend(padding_positions)
                    
                    for idx, pos in enumerate(extra_positions):
                        child[n_to_fill + idx] = pos
            else:  # Balanced approach - mixed set-based with utility guidance
                # Use uniform selection from both parents but with utility weighting
                child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
                
                # For the balanced approach, let's try a different strategy that still considers utilities
                # First, identify positions that appear in both parents
                common_positions = set(parent1) & set(parent2)
                unique_to_parent1 = set(parent1) - set(parent2)
                unique_to_parent2 = set(parent2) - set(parent1)
                
                # Start with common positions (highest confidence)
                pos_idx = 0
                common_list = list(common_positions)
                for pos in common_list[:min(len(common_list), n_decap//3)]:
                    child[pos_idx] = pos
                    pos_idx += 1
                
                # Then mix from both parents based on utilities
                remaining_slots = n_decap - pos_idx
                for slot in range(remaining_slots):
                    # Randomly decide which parent to sample from
                    if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
                        source_set = unique_to_parent1
                    else:
                        source_set = unique_to_parent2
                    
                    # If the source set is empty, switch to the other parent
                    if not source_set:
                        source_set = unique_to_parent2 if source_set == unique_to_parent1 else unique_to_parent1
                    
                    if source_set:
                        # Pick from the source set based on utility weights
                        source_list = list(source_set)
                        source_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in source_list]
                        total_utility = sum(source_utilities)
                        
                        if total_utility > 0:
                            probs = [u / total_utility for u in source_utilities]
                            selected_pos = np.random.choice(source_list, p=probs)
                        else:
                            selected_pos = np.random.choice(source_list)
                        
                        child[pos_idx] = selected_pos
                        pos_idx += 1
                        
                        # Remove this position from both parent sets to avoid duplicates
                        if selected_pos in unique_to_parent1:
                            unique_to_parent1.remove(selected_pos)
                        if selected_pos in unique_to_parent2:
                            unique_to_parent2.remove(selected_pos)
                    else:
                        # If both sets are empty, fill with any available position based on utilities
                        all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size)) - set(child[:pos_idx])
                        if all_positions:
                            all_list = list(all_positions)
                            all_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in all_list]
                            total_utility = sum(all_utilities)
                            
                            if total_utility > 0:
                                probs = [u / total_utility for u in all_utilities]
                                selected_pos = np.random.choice(all_list, p=probs)
                            else:
                                selected_pos = np.random.choice(all_list)
                            
                            child[pos_idx] = selected_pos
                            pos_idx += 1

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements an adaptive crossover operator that dynamically adjusts its strategy based on
    real-time population diversity metrics rather than fixed Jaccard similarity thresholds.
    The algorithm monitors genotype entropy and pairwise Hamming distances across the parent pool
    to determine optimal recombination strategies. When diversity is high, the algorithm favors
    exploration through utility-guided sampling from the union of parent positions. As convergence
    accelerates and diversity decreases, it shifts toward exploitation by preserving common or
    high-frequency positions. This enables organic responses to evolutionary progress instead
    of relying on static heuristics.
    
    The implementation builds on insights from parent solutions by:
    - Computing real-time diversity metrics (genotype entropy and Hamming distances)
    - Using adaptive thresholds that respond to population entropy levels
    - Maintaining multiplicative utility combination (occurrence × spatial importance)
    - Applying spatially-aware duplicate resolution with Manhattan distances
    - Preserving high-confidence common positions when parents are dissimilar
    
    Implementation idea: Replace fixed Jaccard similarity thresholds with adaptive, 
    population-diversity-driven switching criteria by monitoring real-time metrics like 
    genotype entropy or pairwise Hamming distances across the parent pool. Use these 
    dynamic diversity indicators to modulate the recombination strategy—e.g., increasing 
    exploration (utility-guided sampling from union) when diversity is high and shifting 
    toward exploitation (preserving common/high-frequency positions) as convergence accelerates. 
    This enables the crossover operator to respond organically to evolutionary progress 
    rather than relying on static heuristics.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Compute real-time diversity metrics: genotype entropy and Hamming distances
    # Calculate Hamming distances between all parent pairs
    hamming_distances = []
    for i in range(n_parents):
        for j in range(i + 1, n_parents):
            # Count differing positions between two parents
            diff_count = np.sum(parents[i] != parents[j])
            hamming_distances.append(diff_count)
    
    avg_hamming_distance = np.mean(hamming_distances) if hamming_distances else 0.0
    # Normalize Hamming distance to [0, 1] range
    normalized_hamming = avg_hamming_distance / n_decap if n_decap > 0 else 0.0
    
    # Calculate genotype entropy based on position frequencies across all parents
    all_positions = parents.flatten()
    unique_positions, counts = np.unique(all_positions, return_counts=True)
    total_positions = len(all_positions)
    
    # Compute entropy of position distribution
    probs = counts / total_positions
    entropy = -np.sum(probs * np.log2(probs + 1e-10))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
    # Normalize entropy by maximum possible entropy
    max_entropy = np.log2(len(unique_positions)) if len(unique_positions) > 0 else 1.0
    normalized_entropy = entropy / max_entropy if max_entropy > 0 else 0.0
    
    # Determine diversity level based on both metrics
    # High diversity = high entropy AND high normalized Hamming distance
    diversity_metric = (normalized_entropy + normalized_hamming) / 2.0
    
    # Set adaptive thresholds based on diversity metric
    low_diversity_threshold = 0.3  # Lower diversity = more exploitation
    high_diversity_threshold = 0.7  # Higher diversity = more exploration
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence and spatial factors
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner positions
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance using multiplicative combination
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Use multiplicative combination of occurrence and spatial importance
        spatial_normalized = spatial_importance / spatial_importance.max() if spatial_importance.max() > 0 else 1.0
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_normalized
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Generate offspring based on diversity level
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Create union of positions from both parents
        union_positions = list(set(parent1) | set(parent2))
        
        # Based on the diversity level, choose how to construct offspring
        if diversity_metric > high_diversity_threshold:  # High diversity - focus on exploration
            # Build offspring by sampling from the union of parent positions with utility bias
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            used_positions = set()
            
            # First, try to preserve positions that appear in both parents (high-confidence positions)
            common_positions = set(parent1) & set(parent2)
            common_positions_list = list(common_positions)
            np.random.shuffle(common_positions_list)
            
            # Fill some positions with common positions
            n_common_to_use = min(len(common_positions_list), max(1, n_decap // 3))  # Reduce common usage in high diversity
            for idx in range(n_common_to_use):
                child[idx] = common_positions_list[idx]
                used_positions.add(common_positions_list[idx])
            
            # Then sample remaining positions from union based on utility
            remaining_union = [pos for pos in union_positions if pos not in used_positions]
            remaining_count = n_decap - n_common_to_use
            
            if len(remaining_union) >= remaining_count:
                # Sample from remaining union with utility-based probabilities
                remaining_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in remaining_union]
                remaining_sum = sum(remaining_utilities)
                
                if remaining_sum > 0:
                    remaining_probabilities = [u / remaining_sum for u in remaining_utilities]
                    selected_positions = np.random.choice(remaining_union, size=remaining_count, replace=False, p=remaining_probabilities)
                else:
                    selected_positions = np.random.choice(remaining_union, size=remaining_count, replace=False)
            else:
                # Not enough unique positions, so we'll have to add some duplicates initially
                selected_positions = remaining_union[:]
                # Add additional positions from the full grid that aren't in the child yet
                all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                available_positions = list(all_positions - used_positions - set(remaining_union))
                if len(available_positions) > 0:
                    additional_needed = remaining_count - len(remaining_union)
                    additional_count = min(additional_needed, len(available_positions))
                    if additional_count > 0:
                        additional_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_positions]
                        additional_sum = sum(additional_utilities)
                        
                        if additional_sum > 0:
                            additional_probabilities = [u / additional_sum for u in additional_utilities]
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=additional_count, replace=False, p=additional_probabilities)
                        else:
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=additional_count, replace=False)
                        selected_positions.extend(extra_positions)
                
                # Pad with random positions if still short
                if len(selected_positions) < remaining_count:
                    padding_needed = remaining_count - len(selected_positions)
                    all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                    available_for_padding = list(all_positions - set(selected_positions) - used_positions)
                    if len(available_for_padding) >= padding_needed:
                        padding_positions = np.random.choice(available_for_padding, size=padding_needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        # Fallback to allow replacement if not enough unique positions
                        padding_positions = np.random.choice(list(all_positions), size=padding_needed, replace=True)
                    selected_positions.extend(padding_positions)
            
            # Assign the selected positions to the child
            for idx, pos in enumerate(selected_positions):
                child[n_common_to_use + idx] = pos
                
        elif diversity_metric < low_diversity_threshold:  # Low diversity - focus on exploitation
            # Use a set-based approach but favor positions with higher utility
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            used_positions = set()
            
            # Get all positions from both parents
            all_parent_positions = list(parent1) + list(parent2)
            position_freq = Counter(all_parent_positions)
            
            # Sort positions by frequency and utility, preferring those that appear in both parents
            position_scores = []
            for pos in set(all_parent_positions):
                freq_score = position_freq[pos]  # How many times it appears across parents
                utility_score = position_utilities[pos]
                # Prefer positions that appear in both parents, then by utility
                combined_score = freq_score * 10 + utility_score
                position_scores.append((combined_score, pos))
            
            position_scores.sort(reverse=True)
            ranked_positions = [pos for _, pos in position_scores]
            
            # Fill child with highest-ranked positions first
            n_to_fill = min(n_decap, len(ranked_positions))
            for idx in range(n_to_fill):
                child[idx] = ranked_positions[idx]
                used_positions.add(ranked_positions[idx])
            
            # Fill remaining positions from available positions
            if n_to_fill < n_decap:
                all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                available_positions = list(all_positions - used_positions)
                remaining_needed = n_decap - n_to_fill
                
                if len(available_positions) >= remaining_needed:
                    # Select based on utility
                    avail_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_positions]
                    avail_sum = sum(avail_utilities)
                    if avail_sum > 0:
                        avail_probs = [u / avail_sum for u in avail_utilities]
                        extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False, p=avail_probs)
                    else:
                        extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False)
                else:
                    # Not enough unique positions, pad with random
                    extra_positions = available_positions[:]
                    padding_needed = remaining_needed - len(extra_positions)
                    all_remaining = list(set(range(grid_size * grid_size)) - set(extra_positions) - used_positions)
                    if len(all_remaining) >= padding_needed:
                        padding_positions = np.random.choice(all_remaining, size=padding_needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        padding_positions = np.random.choice(range(grid_size * grid_size), size=padding_needed, replace=True)
                    extra_positions.extend(padding_positions)
                
                for idx, pos in enumerate(extra_positions):
                    child[n_to_fill + idx] = pos
        else:  # Medium diversity - balanced approach
            # Use uniform selection from both parents but with utility weighting
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            
            # Mix of common positions and utility-guided selection
            common_positions = set(parent1) & set(parent2)
            n_common_to_use = min(len(common_positions), max(1, n_decap // 4))
            
            # Add common positions first
            common_list = list(common_positions)
            for idx in range(min(n_common_to_use, len(common_list))):
                child[idx] = common_list[idx]
            
            # For remaining positions, alternate between parents with utility guidance
            for idx in range(n_common_to_use, n_decap):
                # Choose which parent to inherit from with slight bias towards parent with higher utility positions
                if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
                    source_positions = parent1
                else:
                    source_positions = parent2
                
                # Randomly pick a position from the chosen parent but with utility weighting
                # Calculate utilities for positions in the selected parent
                parent_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in source_positions]
                parent_sum = sum(parent_utilities)
                
                if parent_sum > 0:
                    parent_probs = [u / parent_sum for u in parent_utilities]
                    selected_pos = np.random.choice(source_positions, p=parent_probs)
                else:
                    selected_pos = np.random.choice(source_positions)
                
                child[idx] = selected_pos
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    if selected_pos in available_positions:
                        available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements a set-based uniform crossover that treats decap placements as unordered sets.
    Uses Jaccard similarity to adaptively choose between different recombination strategies:
    - Low similarity: Preserve common positions between parents
    - Medium similarity: Balanced approach sampling from both parents
    - High similarity: Explore more diverse positions from union of parents
    
    The implementation uses multiplicative utility combination (occurrence × spatial importance)
    and spatially-aware duplicate resolution with Manhattan distances.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence and spatial factors
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner positions
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance using multiplicative combination
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Use multiplicative combination of occurrence and spatial importance
        spatial_normalized = spatial_importance / spatial_importance.max() if spatial_importance.max() > 0 else 1.0
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_normalized
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Define fixed thresholds based on parent solution success
    low_similarity_threshold = 0.25
    high_similarity_threshold = 0.55
    
    # Generate offspring
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Calculate Jaccard similarity between parents
        set1, set2 = set(parent1), set(parent2)
        intersection = len(set1 & set2)
        union = len(set1 | set2)
        jaccard_similarity = intersection / union if union > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Based on similarity, choose how to construct offspring
        if jaccard_similarity < low_similarity_threshold:  # Low similarity - preserve common positions
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            
            # First, preserve all common positions between parents
            common_positions = list(set1 & set2)
            n_common = len(common_positions)
            
            # Fill child with common positions first
            for idx in range(min(n_common, n_decap)):
                child[idx] = common_positions[idx]
            
            # For remaining positions, use positions from both parents based on utility
            used_positions = set(common_positions)
            remaining_positions = []
            
            # Collect positions from both parents that are not already used
            for pos in parent1:
                if pos not in used_positions and pos not in remaining_positions:
                    remaining_positions.append(pos)
            for pos in parent2:
                if pos not in used_positions and pos not in remaining_positions:
                    remaining_positions.append(pos)
            
            # Fill remaining slots with positions from the union based on utility
            remaining_count = n_decap - n_common
            if remaining_count > 0 and remaining_positions:
                if len(remaining_positions) >= remaining_count:
                    # Select from remaining positions with utility bias
                    remaining_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in remaining_positions]
                    remaining_sum = sum(remaining_utilities)
                    if remaining_sum > 0:
                        remaining_probabilities = [u / remaining_sum for u in remaining_utilities]
                        selected_remaining = np.random.choice(remaining_positions, size=remaining_count, replace=False, p=remaining_probabilities)
                    else:
                        selected_remaining = np.random.choice(remaining_positions, size=remaining_count, replace=False)
                else:
                    # Not enough unique positions, use what we have and add others
                    selected_remaining = remaining_positions[:]
                    # Add more positions from the full grid that aren't used yet
                    all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                    available = list(all_positions - used_positions - set(remaining_positions))
                    needed = remaining_count - len(selected_remaining)
                    if available and needed > 0:
                        if len(available) >= needed:
                            available_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available]
                            available_sum = sum(available_utilities)
                            if available_sum > 0:
                                available_probabilities = [u / available_sum for u in available_utilities]
                                extra_positions = np.random.choice(available, size=needed, replace=False, p=available_probabilities)
                            else:
                                extra_positions = np.random.choice(available, size=needed, replace=False)
                        else:
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available, size=len(available), replace=False)
                        selected_remaining = np.concatenate([selected_remaining, extra_positions])
                
                # Assign to child
                for idx, pos in enumerate(selected_remaining[:remaining_count]):
                    child[n_common + idx] = pos
            
            # If still not filled, pad with random positions
            if n_common + len(selected_remaining) < n_decap:
                all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                currently_used = set(child[:n_common + len(selected_remaining)])
                available = list(all_positions - currently_used)
                if available:
                    padding_needed = n_decap - (n_common + len(selected_remaining))
                    if len(available) >= padding_needed:
                        child[n_common + len(selected_remaining):n_decap] = np.random.choice(available, size=padding_needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        # Use with replacement if not enough unique positions
                        child[n_common + len(selected_remaining):n_decap] = np.random.choice(available, size=padding_needed, replace=True)
        
        elif jaccard_similarity > high_similarity_threshold:  # High similarity - encourage diversity
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            
            # Start with all positions from both parents
            union_positions = list(set1 | set2)
            np.random.shuffle(union_positions)
            
            # Use as many union positions as possible
            n_union = min(len(union_positions), n_decap)
            for idx in range(n_union):
                child[idx] = union_positions[idx]
            
            # For remaining positions, try to add positions that are not in either parent
            if n_union < n_decap:
                used_so_far = set(union_positions[:n_union])
                all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                available_positions = list(all_positions - set1 - set2 - used_so_far)
                
                if available_positions:
                    remaining_needed = n_decap - n_union
                    if len(available_positions) >= remaining_needed:
                        # Select based on utility
                        available_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_positions]
                        available_sum = sum(available_utilities)
                        if available_sum > 0:
                            available_probabilities = [u / available_sum for u in available_utilities]
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False, p=available_probabilities)
                        else:
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        extra_positions = available_positions[:]
                        # Add more if needed
                        remaining_after_available = remaining_needed - len(extra_positions)
                        if remaining_after_available > 0:
                            other_unused = list(all_positions - set(extra_positions) - set(union_positions[:n_union]))
                            if len(other_unused) >= remaining_after_available:
                                more_positions = np.random.choice(other_unused, size=remaining_after_available, replace=False)
                            else:
                                more_positions = np.random.choice(range(grid_size * grid_size), size=remaining_after_available, replace=True)
                            extra_positions = np.concatenate([extra_positions, more_positions])
                    
                    for idx, pos in enumerate(extra_positions):
                        child[n_union + idx] = pos
        
        else:  # Medium similarity - balanced approach
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            
            # Start with common positions
            common_positions = list(set1 & set2)
            n_common = min(len(common_positions), max(1, n_decap // 4))  # Use up to 1/4 for common
            for idx in range(n_common):
                child[idx] = common_positions[idx]
            
            # For remaining positions, alternate between parents with utility bias
            used_positions = set(common_positions)
            for idx in range(n_common, n_decap):
                # Randomly choose parent
                if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
                    source_parent = parent1
                else:
                    source_parent = parent2
                
                # Get positions from source parent that haven't been used
                available_from_source = [pos for pos in source_parent if pos not in used_positions]
                
                if available_from_source:
                    # Use utility to select from available positions
                    source_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_from_source]
                    source_sum = sum(source_utilities)
                    if source_sum > 0:
                        source_probs = [u / source_sum for u in source_utilities]
                        selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_from_source, p=source_probs)
                    else:
                        selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_from_source)
                else:
                    # If all positions from source are used, pick from all unused positions
                    all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                    available_all = list(all_positions - used_positions)
                    if available_all:
                        available_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_all]
                        available_sum = sum(available_utilities)
                        if available_sum > 0:
                            available_probs = [u / available_sum for u in available_utilities]
                            selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_all, p=available_probs)
                        else:
                            selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_all)
                    else:
                        # Fallback to any random position
                        selected_pos = np.random.randint(0, grid_size * grid_size)
                
                child[idx] = selected_pos
                used_positions.add(selected_pos)
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    if selected_pos in available_positions:
                        available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements a set-based uniform crossover that treats decap placements as unordered sets.
    Uses Jaccard similarity to adaptively choose between different recombination strategies:
    - Low similarity: Preserve common positions between parents
    - Medium similarity: Balanced approach sampling from both parents
    - High similarity: Explore more diverse positions from union of parents
    
    The implementation uses multiplicative utility combination (occurrence × spatial importance)
    and spatially-aware duplicate resolution with Manhattan distances.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence and spatial factors
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner positions
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance using multiplicative combination
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Use multiplicative combination of occurrence and spatial importance
        spatial_normalized = spatial_importance / spatial_importance.max() if spatial_importance.max() > 0 else 1.0
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_normalized
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)

    low_similarity_threshold = 0.25
    high_similarity_threshold = 0.55

    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]

        set1, set2 = set(parent1), set(parent2)
        intersection = len(set1 & set2)
        union = len(set1 | set2)
        jaccard_similarity = intersection / union if union > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Based on similarity, choose how to construct offspring
        if jaccard_similarity < low_similarity_threshold:  # Low similarity - preserve common positions
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            
            # First, preserve all common positions between parents
            common_positions = list(set1 & set2)
            n_common = len(common_positions)
            
            # Fill child with common positions first
            for idx in range(min(n_common, n_decap)):
                child[idx] = common_positions[idx]
            
            # For remaining positions, use positions from both parents based on utility
            used_positions = set(common_positions)
            remaining_positions = []
            
            # Collect positions from both parents that are not already used
            for pos in parent1:
                if pos not in used_positions and pos not in remaining_positions:
                    remaining_positions.append(pos)
            for pos in parent2:
                if pos not in used_positions and pos not in remaining_positions:
                    remaining_positions.append(pos)

            remaining_count = n_decap - n_common
            if remaining_count > 0 and remaining_positions:
                if len(remaining_positions) >= remaining_count:
                    # Select from remaining positions with utility bias
                    remaining_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in remaining_positions]
                    remaining_sum = sum(remaining_utilities)
                    if remaining_sum > 0:
                        remaining_probabilities = [u / remaining_sum for u in remaining_utilities]
                        selected_remaining = np.random.choice(remaining_positions, size=remaining_count, replace=False, p=remaining_probabilities)
                    else:
                        selected_remaining = np.random.choice(remaining_positions, size=remaining_count, replace=False)
                else:
                    # Not enough unique positions, use what we have and add others
                    selected_remaining = remaining_positions[:]
                    # Add more positions from the full grid that aren't used yet
                    all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                    available = list(all_positions - used_positions - set(remaining_positions))
                    needed = remaining_count - len(selected_remaining)
                    if available and needed > 0:
                        if len(available) >= needed:
                            available_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available]
                            available_sum = sum(available_utilities)
                            if available_sum > 0:
                                available_probabilities = [u / available_sum for u in available_utilities]
                                extra_positions = np.random.choice(available, size=needed, replace=False, p=available_probabilities)
                            else:
                                extra_positions = np.random.choice(available, size=needed, replace=False)
                        else:
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available, size=len(available), replace=False)
                        selected_remaining = np.concatenate([selected_remaining, extra_positions])
                
                # Assign to child
                for idx, pos in enumerate(selected_remaining[:remaining_count]):
                    child[n_common + idx] = pos
            
            # If still not filled, pad with random positions
            if n_common + len(selected_remaining) < n_decap:
                all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                currently_used = set(child[:n_common + len(selected_remaining)])
                available = list(all_positions - currently_used)
                if available:
                    padding_needed = n_decap - (n_common + len(selected_remaining))
                    if len(available) >= padding_needed:
                        child[n_common + len(selected_remaining):n_decap] = np.random.choice(available, size=padding_needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        # Use with replacement if not enough unique positions
                        child[n_common + len(selected_remaining):n_decap] = np.random.choice(available, size=padding_needed, replace=True)
        
        elif jaccard_similarity > high_similarity_threshold:  # High similarity - encourage diversity
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            
            # Start with all positions from both parents
            union_positions = list(set1 | set2)
            np.random.shuffle(union_positions)
            
            # Use as many union positions as possible
            n_union = min(len(union_positions), n_decap)
            for idx in range(n_union):
                child[idx] = union_positions[idx]

            if n_union < n_decap:
                used_so_far = set(union_positions[:n_union])
                all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                available_positions = list(all_positions - set1 - set2 - used_so_far)

                    remaining_needed = n_decap - n_union
                    if len(available_positions) >= remaining_needed:
