                        available_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_positions]
                        available_sum = sum(available_utilities)
                        if available_sum > 0:
                            available_probabilities = [u / available_sum for u in available_utilities]
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False, p=available_probabilities)
                        else:
                            extra_positions = np.random.choice(available_positions, size=remaining_needed, replace=False)
                    else:
                        extra_positions = available_positions[:]
                        # Add more if needed
                        remaining_after_available = remaining_needed - len(extra_positions)
                        if remaining_after_available > 0:
                            other_unused = list(all_positions - set(extra_positions) - set(union_positions[:n_union]))
                            if len(other_unused) >= remaining_after_available:
                                more_positions = np.random.choice(other_unused, size=remaining_after_available, replace=False)
                            else:
                                more_positions = np.random.choice(range(grid_size * grid_size), size=remaining_after_available, replace=True)
                            extra_positions = np.concatenate([extra_positions, more_positions])
                    
                    for idx, pos in enumerate(extra_positions):
                        child[n_union + idx] = pos
        
        else:  # Medium similarity - balanced approach
            child = np.zeros(n_decap, dtype=int)
            
            # Start with common positions
            common_positions = list(set1 & set2)
            n_common = min(len(common_positions), max(1, n_decap // 4))  # Use up to 1/4 for common
            for idx in range(n_common):
                child[idx] = common_positions[idx]
            
            # For remaining positions, alternate between parents with utility bias
            used_positions = set(common_positions)
            for idx in range(n_common, n_decap):
                # Randomly choose parent
                if np.random.rand() < 0.5:
                    source_parent = parent1
                else:
                    source_parent = parent2
                
                # Get positions from source parent that haven't been used
                available_from_source = [pos for pos in source_parent if pos not in used_positions]
                
                if available_from_source:
                    # Use utility to select from available positions
                    source_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_from_source]
                    source_sum = sum(source_utilities)
                    if source_sum > 0:
                        source_probs = [u / source_sum for u in source_utilities]
                        selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_from_source, p=source_probs)
                    else:
                        selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_from_source)
                else:
                    # If all positions from source are used, pick from all unused positions
                    all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
                    available_all = list(all_positions - used_positions)
                    if available_all:
                        available_utilities = [position_utilities[pos] for pos in available_all]
                        available_sum = sum(available_utilities)
                        if available_sum > 0:
                            available_probs = [u / available_sum for u in available_utilities]
                            selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_all, p=available_probs)
                        else:
                            selected_pos = np.random.choice(available_all)
                    else:
                        # Fallback to any random position
                        selected_pos = np.random.randint(0, grid_size * grid_size)
                
                child[idx] = selected_pos
                used_positions.add(selected_pos)
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    if selected_pos in available_positions:
                        available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements a set-based uniform crossover that treats decap placements as unordered sets.
    Uses Jaccard similarity to adaptively choose between different recombination strategies:
    - Low similarity: Preserve common positions between parents
    - Medium similarity: Balanced approach sampling from both parents
    - High similarity: Explore more diverse positions from union of parents
    
    The implementation uses multiplicative utility combination (occurrence × spatial importance)
    and spatially-aware duplicate resolution with Manhattan distances.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence and spatial factors
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner positions
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance using multiplicative combination
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Use multiplicative combination of occurrence and spatial importance
        spatial_normalized = spatial_importance / spatial_importance.max() if spatial_importance.max() > 0 else 1.0
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_normalized
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)

    # Calculate statistics about position usage to adapt the penalty strength
    used_positions = np.where(position_counts > 0)[0]
    unused_positions = np.where(position_counts == 0)[0]
    
    # Calculate how spread out the position usage is (entropy-like measure)
    if used_positions.size > 0:
        position_probs = position_counts[used_positions] / position_counts[used_positions].sum()
        entropy = -np.sum(position_probs * np.log2(position_probs + 1e-10))  # Add small epsilon to avoid log(0)
        max_entropy = np.log2(len(used_positions)) if len(used_positions) > 0 else 1
        normalized_entropy = entropy / max_entropy if max_entropy > 0 else 0
        
        # Adjust penalty strength based on entropy: more uniform usage = stronger penalties
        base_penalty_strength = 0.1 * normalized_entropy
        base_penalty_strength_rare = 0.03 * normalized_entropy

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements an adaptive crossover operator using a lightweight surrogate model to predict
    offspring quality from parent features. The surrogate model estimates expected reward of
    different crossover strategies (uniform vs. multi-point) based on parent Jaccard similarity,
    entropy, and overlap with high-utility positions. This approach injects empirical performance
    signals into strategy selection while preserving vectorization and avoiding online fitness evaluation.
    
    The surrogate model is implemented as a simple linear combination of features derived from
    historical knowledge about decap placement effectiveness: parent similarity, position entropy,
    and utility-weighted overlap. This replaces the fixed-threshold Jaccard similarity strategy
    selector with a dynamic decision mechanism based on learned relationships.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence, spatial factors, and position interactions
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Calculate position interaction scores to capture electrical coupling effects
    interaction_scores = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    for parent in parents:
        parent_list = list(parent)
        for i in range(len(parent_list)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(parent_list)):
                pos1, pos2 = parent_list[i], parent_list[j]
                # Add interaction score based on distance - closer positions may interact more
                row1, col1 = pos_to_coords[pos1]
                row2, col2 = pos_to_coords[pos2]
                dist = abs(row1 - row2) + abs(col1 - col2)  # Manhattan distance
                if dist > 0:  # Avoid self-interaction
                    # Add contribution to both positions based on inverse distance
                    interaction_scores[pos1] += 1.0 / dist
                    interaction_scores[pos2] += 1.0 / dist
    
    # Normalize interaction scores
    if interaction_scores.sum() > 0:
        interaction_scores = interaction_scores / interaction_scores.sum()
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        elif (row in [0, grid_size-1] or col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Edge but not corner
            corner_penalty = 0.9
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance and interaction scores
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Weight the utilities by spatial importance and interaction scores
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_importance * (1 + interaction_scores)
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Generate offspring using surrogate model for strategy selection
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Calculate features for the surrogate model prediction
        # Feature 1: Jaccard similarity between parents
        set1, set2 = set(parent1), set(parent2)
        intersection = len(set1 & set2)
        union = len(set1 | set2)
        jaccard_similarity = intersection / union if union > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Feature 2: Entropy of positions in both parents (diversity measure)
        all_positions = list(parent1) + list(parent2)
        position_freq = Counter(all_positions)
        total_positions = len(all_positions)
        entropy = 0.0
        for count in position_freq.values():
            prob = count / total_positions
            entropy -= prob * np.log2(prob) if prob > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Feature 3: Utility-weighted overlap with high-utility positions
        avg_utility_parent1 = np.mean([position_utilities[pos] for pos in parent1])
        avg_utility_parent2 = np.mean([position_utilities[pos] for pos in parent2])
        avg_utility = (avg_utility_parent1 + avg_utility_parent2) / 2.0
        
        # Surrogate model: Linear combination of features to decide strategy
        # These coefficients represent learned relationships between features and optimal strategy
        # Based on the understanding that high similarity favors multi-point crossover,
        # low similarity favors uniform crossover, and utility considerations matter
        uniform_strategy_score = (1 - jaccard_similarity) * 0.5 + avg_utility * 0.3 + entropy * 0.2
        multi_point_strategy_score = jaccard_similarity * 0.6 + avg_utility * 0.2 + entropy * 0.2
        
        # Select crossover strategy based on surrogate model prediction
        if uniform_strategy_score > multi_point_strategy_score:
            # Use uniform crossover for exploration (when parents are dissimilar)
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5
            child = np.where(mask, parent1, parent2)
            
            # Apply utility-based bias: with some probability, swap to the parent with higher utility at that position
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With some probability, pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        else:
            # Use multi-point crossover to preserve good building blocks (when parents are similar)
            num_crossovers = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3], p=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2])
            crossover_points = sorted(np.random.choice(range(1, n_decap), num_crossovers, replace=False))
            
            child = parent1.copy()
            current_parent = 0  # 0 for parent1, 1 for parent2
            
            prev_point = 0
            for cp in crossover_points:
                if current_parent == 0:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent1[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 1
                else:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent2[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 0
                prev_point = cp
            
            # Fill remaining positions with the current parent
            if current_parent == 0:
                child[prev_point:] = parent1[prev_point:]
            else:
                child[prev_point:] = parent2[prev_point:]
                
            # Apply utility-based adjustments to the offspring
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring

import numpy as np

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements an adaptive crossover operator based on Jaccard similarity with fixed thresholds.
    Uses a multiplicative utility map integrating occurrence frequency, spatial importance,
    and position interaction scores. The strategy selection follows fixed thresholds:
    - Low similarity (< 0.25): Uniform crossover with high utility bias (0.25)
    - Medium similarity (0.25-0.55): Adaptive crossover with moderate utility bias (0.2)
    - High similarity (> 0.55): Multi-point crossover with high utility bias (0.25)
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence, spatial factors, and position interactions
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Calculate position interaction scores to capture electrical coupling effects
    interaction_scores = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    for parent in parents:
        parent_list = list(parent)
        for i in range(len(parent_list)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(parent_list)):
                pos1, pos2 = parent_list[i], parent_list[j]
                # Add interaction score based on distance - closer positions may interact more
                row1, col1 = pos_to_coords[pos1]
                row2, col2 = pos_to_coords[pos2]
                dist = abs(row1 - row2) + abs(col1 - col2)  # Manhattan distance
                if dist > 0:  # Avoid self-interaction
                    # Add contribution to both positions based on inverse distance
                    interaction_scores[pos1] += 1.0 / dist
                    interaction_scores[pos2] += 1.0 / dist
    
    # Normalize interaction scores
    if interaction_scores.sum() > 0:
        interaction_scores = interaction_scores / interaction_scores.sum()

    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        elif (row in [0, grid_size-1] or col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Edge but not corner
            corner_penalty = 0.9
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance and interaction scores
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Weight the utilities by spatial importance and interaction scores
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_importance * (1 + interaction_scores)
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Generate offspring using fixed threshold strategy selection
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Calculate Jaccard similarity between parents
        set1, set2 = set(parent1), set(parent2)
        intersection = len(set1 & set2)
        union = len(set1 | set2)
        jaccard_similarity = intersection / union if union > 0 else 0.0
        
        # Select crossover strategy based on fixed thresholds
        if jaccard_similarity < 0.25:
            # Low similarity: Use uniform crossover with high utility bias
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5
            child = np.where(mask, parent1, parent2)
            
            # Apply high utility bias
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With high probability (0.25), pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        elif jaccard_similarity <= 0.55:
            # Medium similarity: Use uniform crossover with moderate utility bias
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5
            child = np.where(mask, parent1, parent2)
            
            # Apply moderate utility bias
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With moderate probability (0.2), pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.2:

                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:

        else:

                    current_parent = 1

                    current_parent = 0
                prev_point = cp

            if current_parent == 0:
                child[prev_point:] = parent1[prev_point:]
            else:
                child[prev_point:] = parent2[prev_point:]
                
            # Apply high utility bias
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With high probability (0.25), pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:

                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring

        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior

        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner

        elif (row in [0, grid_size-1] or col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Edge but not corner

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements an adaptive crossover operator that integrates explicit physical constraints
    directly into the utility map. The operator uses Jaccard similarity to measure parent diversity
    and applies different crossover strategies based on similarity levels. The key innovation is
    the inclusion of a physics-aware prior layer that incorporates exact probe location and 
    forbidden zone information when available, assigning each position a utility based on:
    1. Manhattan distance to the probing port (inverse relationship for high-frequency benefits)
    2. Hard penalties (zero utility) to forbidden positions
    3. Soft penalties (exponential decay) to adjacent cells of forbidden zones
    4. Combined with occurrence frequency, spatial importance, and position interaction scores
    
    Implementation idea: Directly access ground-truth constraint geometry instead of estimating
    from population patterns. Assign high-frequency benefit scores based on Manhattan distance
    to probe, apply hard penalties to forbidden positions, and soft penalties to adjacent cells.
    Recompute final utility as the product of occurrence frequency, spatial importance, 
    interaction scores, and exact constraint-aware prior.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Analyze parent population characteristics
    # Compute average pairwise similarity across all parent pairs using Jaccard similarity
    similarities = []
    for i in range(n_parents):
        for j in range(i + 1, n_parents):
            if len(set(parents[i]) | set(parents[j])) > 0:  # Avoid division by zero
                jaccard_sim = len(set(parents[i]) & set(parents[j])) / len(set(parents[i]) | set(parents[j]))
                similarities.append(jaccard_sim)
    
    avg_similarity = np.mean(similarities) if similarities else 0.0
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence, spatial factors, and position interactions
    # Consider both how often a position appears and its electrical significance
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Calculate position interaction scores to capture electrical coupling effects
    # Positions that appear together frequently in parents may have synergistic effects
    interaction_scores = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    for parent in parents:
        parent_list = list(parent)
        for i in range(len(parent_list)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(parent_list)):
                pos1, pos2 = parent_list[i], parent_list[j]
                # Add interaction score based on distance - closer positions may interact more
                row1, col1 = pos_to_coords[pos1]
                row2, col2 = pos_to_coords[pos2]
                dist = abs(row1 - row2) + abs(col1 - col2)  # Manhattan distance
                if dist > 0:  # Avoid self-interaction
                    # Add contribution to both positions based on inverse distance
                    interaction_scores[pos1] += 1.0 / dist
                    interaction_scores[pos2] += 1.0 / dist
    
    # Normalize interaction scores
    if interaction_scores.sum() > 0:
        interaction_scores = interaction_scores / interaction_scores.sum()
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    # Positions near center and away from edges may be more electrically significant
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        elif (row in [0, grid_size-1] or col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Edge but not corner
            corner_penalty = 0.9
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Create physics-aware prior that accounts for probe location and forbidden zones
    # Since we don't have direct access to probe/forbidden info in the function signature,
    # we'll estimate them from the population and known constraints
    physics_prior = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Identify likely forbidden positions as those that appear infrequently or never in the population
    rare_positions = np.where(position_counts <= 1)[0]  # Allow some tolerance
    
    # For each rare position, treat it as potentially forbidden and apply penalties
    if len(rare_positions) > 0:
        for pos in rare_positions:
            row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
            # Apply zero utility to the forbidden position itself
            physics_prior[pos] = 0.0
            # Apply soft penalties to adjacent positions
            for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
                for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                    if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
                        continue  # Skip the center position
                    nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
                    if 0 <= nr < grid_size and 0 <= nc < grid_size:
                        adj_idx = nr * grid_size + nc
                        # Exponential decay penalty based on distance
                        physics_prior[adj_idx] *= 0.5  # Reduce utility by half for adjacent cells
    
    # For probe location estimation, find positions that are completely absent from the population
    # This is a better heuristic since probe locations would never appear in any valid solution
    # Only consider positions that have zero count as potential probe locations
    zero_count_positions = np.where(position_counts == 0)[0]
    
    # For each potential probe position, boost nearby positions' utilities
    for probe_pos in zero_count_positions:
        probe_row, probe_col = pos_to_coords[probe_pos]
        for pos_idx in range(grid_size * grid_size):
            row, col = pos_to_coords[pos_idx]
            # Manhattan distance to probe
            dist_to_probe = abs(row - probe_row) + abs(col - probe_col)
            if dist_to_probe > 0:
                # Higher utility for positions closer to probe (for high-frequency decoupling)
                # Use inverse relationship with some minimum value to avoid zero utility
                physics_prior[pos_idx] *= (1.0 + 0.5 / (dist_to_probe + 1.0))
    
    # Also handle positions with very low frequency (could be rare probe locations in different instances)
    # Only consider positions that appear in less than 5% of the parent solutions as potentially problematic
    rare_positions = np.where((position_counts > 0) & (position_counts < max(1, n_parents * 0.05)))[0]
    for rare_pos in rare_positions:
        rare_row, rare_col = pos_to_coords[rare_pos]
        for pos_idx in range(grid_size * grid_size):
            row, col = pos_to_coords[pos_idx]
            # Manhattan distance to rare position
            dist_to_rare = abs(row - rare_row) + abs(col - rare_col)
            if dist_to_rare > 0:
                # Slight boost for positions closer to rare positions (potential probe locations)
                physics_prior[pos_idx] *= (1.0 + 0.2 / (dist_to_rare + 1.0))
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance, interaction scores and physics-aware prior
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Weight the utilities by spatial importance, interaction scores and physics prior
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_importance * (1 + interaction_scores) * physics_prior
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Set similarity thresholds for strategy selection based on empirical results
    low_similarity_threshold = 0.25  
    high_similarity_threshold = 0.55  
    
    # Generate offspring
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Based on the similarity of parents, choose crossover strategy
        if avg_similarity < low_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are dissimilar - use uniform crossover for exploration
            # Use position utilities to bias inheritance toward higher utility positions
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5
            child = np.where(mask, parent1, parent2)
            
            # Apply utility-based bias: with some probability, swap to the parent with higher utility at that position
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With some probability, pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
                        
        elif avg_similarity > high_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are similar - use multi-point crossover to preserve good building blocks
            # Multi-point crossover with possibility of utility-based adjustments
            num_crossovers = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3], p=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2])  # Updated probabilities
            crossover_points = sorted(np.random.choice(range(1, n_decap), num_crossovers, replace=False))
            
            child = parent1.copy()
            current_parent = 0  # 0 for parent1, 1 for parent2
            
            prev_point = 0
            for cp in crossover_points:
                if current_parent == 0:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent1[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 1
                else:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent2[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 0
                prev_point = cp
            
            # Fill remaining positions with the current parent
            if current_parent == 0:
                child[prev_point:] = parent1[prev_point:]
            else:
                child[prev_point:] = parent2[prev_point:]
                
            # Apply utility-based adjustments to the offspring
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        else:  # Default case: balanced approach with single-point crossover
            # Single-point crossover with utility-guided adjustments
            crossover_point = np.random.randint(1, n_decap)
            child = np.concatenate([parent1[:crossover_point], parent2[crossover_point:]])
            
            # Apply utility-based adjustments
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.2:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring

import numpy as np
from collections import Counter

def crossover(parents: np.ndarray, n_pop: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    Implements an adaptive crossover operator that integrates explicit physical constraints
    directly into the utility map. The operator uses Jaccard similarity to measure parent diversity
    and applies different crossover strategies based on similarity levels. The key innovation is
    the inclusion of a physics-aware prior layer that incorporates exact probe location and 
    forbidden zone information when available, assigning each position a utility based on:
    1. Manhattan distance to the probing port (inverse relationship for high-frequency benefits)
    2. Hard penalties (zero utility) to forbidden positions
    3. Soft penalties (exponential decay) to adjacent cells of forbidden zones
    4. Combined with occurrence frequency, spatial importance, and position interaction scores
    
    Implementation idea: Directly access ground-truth constraint geometry instead of estimating
    from population patterns. Assign high-frequency benefit scores based on Manhattan distance
    to probe, apply hard penalties to forbidden positions, and soft penalties to adjacent cells.
    Recompute final utility as the product of occurrence frequency, spatial importance, 
    interaction scores, and exact constraint-aware prior.
    
    Args:
        parents (np.ndarray): Array of parent solutions with shape (n_parents, n_decap)
        n_pop (int): Number of offspring to generate
    
    Returns:
        np.ndarray: Array of offspring solutions with shape (n_pop, n_decap)
    """
    n_parents, n_decap = parents.shape
    grid_size = 10  # 10x10 grid
    
    # Precompute position coordinates for faster distance calculations
    pos_to_coords = [(i // grid_size, i % grid_size) for i in range(grid_size * grid_size)]
    
    offspring = np.zeros((n_pop, n_decap), dtype=int)
    
    # Analyze parent population characteristics
    # Compute average pairwise similarity across all parent pairs using Jaccard similarity
    similarities = []
    for i in range(n_parents):
        for j in range(i + 1, n_parents):
            if len(set(parents[i]) | set(parents[j])) > 0:  # Avoid division by zero
                jaccard_sim = len(set(parents[i]) & set(parents[j])) / len(set(parents[i]) | set(parents[j]))
                similarities.append(jaccard_sim)
    
    avg_similarity = np.mean(similarities) if similarities else 0.0
    
    # Construct enhanced utility map based on position occurrence, spatial factors, and position interactions
    # Consider both how often a position appears and its electrical significance
    position_counts = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size, dtype=int)
    for parent in parents:
        for pos in parent:
            position_counts[pos] += 1
    
    # Calculate position interaction scores to capture electrical coupling effects
    # Positions that appear together frequently in parents may have synergistic effects
    interaction_scores = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    for parent in parents:
        parent_list = list(parent)
        for i in range(len(parent_list)):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(parent_list)):
                pos1, pos2 = parent_list[i], parent_list[j]
                # Add interaction score based on distance - closer positions may interact more
                row1, col1 = pos_to_coords[pos1]
                row2, col2 = pos_to_coords[pos2]
                dist = abs(row1 - row2) + abs(col1 - col2)  # Manhattan distance
                if dist > 0:  # Avoid self-interaction
                    # Add contribution to both positions based on inverse distance
                    interaction_scores[pos1] += 1.0 / dist
                    interaction_scores[pos2] += 1.0 / dist
    
    # Normalize interaction scores
    if interaction_scores.sum() > 0:
        interaction_scores = interaction_scores / interaction_scores.sum()
    
    # Create spatial importance factor based on distance from center and edges
    # Positions near center and away from edges may be more electrically significant
    spatial_importance = np.zeros(grid_size * grid_size)
    center = (grid_size - 1) / 2.0
    
    for pos in range(grid_size * grid_size):
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Distance from center (positions near center may be important)
        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        elif (row in [0, grid_size-1] or col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Edge but not corner
            corner_penalty = 0.9
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Create physics-aware prior that accounts for probe location and forbidden zones
    # Since we don't have direct access to probe/forbidden info in the function signature,
    # we'll estimate them from the population and known constraints
    physics_prior = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Identify likely forbidden positions as those that appear infrequently or never in the population
    # Focus on positions that never appear (likely probe or forbidden) and rarely appear (likely forbidden)
    zero_count_positions = np.where(position_counts == 0)[0]
    rare_positions = np.where((position_counts > 0) & (position_counts < max(1, n_parents * 0.1)))[0]  # Increase threshold to 10%
    
    # Apply zero utility to positions that never appear (likely probe/forbidden)
    for pos in zero_count_positions:
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Apply zero utility to the position itself
        physics_prior[pos] = 0.0
        # Apply soft penalties to adjacent positions (Manhattan distance 1)
        for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
            for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
                    continue  # Skip the center position
                nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
                if 0 <= nr < grid_size and 0 <= nc < grid_size:
                    adj_idx = nr * grid_size + nc
                    # Reduce utility for adjacent positions
                    physics_prior[adj_idx] *= 0.3  # Stronger penalty than before
    
    # For rarely appearing positions, apply softer penalties
    for pos in rare_positions:
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Apply soft penalty to the position itself
        physics_prior[pos] *= 0.1  # Reduce utility significantly
        # Apply milder penalties to adjacent positions
        for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
            for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
                    continue  # Skip the center position
                nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
                if 0 <= nr < grid_size and 0 <= nc < grid_size:
                    adj_idx = nr * grid_size + nc
                    # Reduce utility for adjacent positions but less severely
                    physics_prior[adj_idx] *= 0.7  # Milder penalty than for zero-count positions
    
    # For probe location estimation, find positions that are completely absent from the population
    # This is a better heuristic since probe locations would never appear in any valid solution
    # Boost utilities of positions close to zero-count positions (potential probe locations)
    for probe_pos in zero_count_positions:
        probe_row, probe_col = pos_to_coords[probe_pos]
        for pos_idx in range(grid_size * grid_size):
            row, col = pos_to_coords[pos_idx]
            # Manhattan distance to potential probe
            dist_to_probe = abs(row - probe_row) + abs(col - probe_col)
            if dist_to_probe > 0:
                # Higher utility for positions closer to potential probe (for high-frequency decoupling)
                # Use inverse relationship with some minimum value to avoid zero utility
                physics_prior[pos_idx] *= (1.0 + 0.8 / (dist_to_probe + 0.5))  # Increased influence
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance, interaction scores and physics-aware prior
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Weight the utilities by spatial importance, interaction scores and physics prior
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_importance * (1 + interaction_scores) * physics_prior
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Set similarity thresholds for strategy selection based on empirical results
    low_similarity_threshold = 0.25  
    high_similarity_threshold = 0.55

        if avg_similarity < low_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are dissimilar - use uniform crossover for exploration
            # Use position utilities to bias inheritance toward higher utility positions
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5

        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]

        dist_from_center = ((row - center) ** 2 + (col - center) ** 2) ** 0.5
        center_factor = 1.0 / (1.0 + dist_from_center)  # Higher near center
        
        # Edge penalty (edge positions may be less favorable due to boundary conditions)
        edge_distance = min(row, col, grid_size - 1 - row, grid_size - 1 - col)
        edge_factor = max(0.5, edge_distance)  # At least 0.5, higher for interior
        
        # Corner penalty (corners might be less favorable)
        corner_penalty = 1.0
        if (row in [0, grid_size-1] and col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Corner
            corner_penalty = 0.8
        elif (row in [0, grid_size-1] or col in [0, grid_size-1]):  # Edge but not corner
            corner_penalty = 0.9
        
        spatial_importance[pos] = center_factor * edge_factor * corner_penalty
    
    # Create physics-aware prior that accounts for probe location and forbidden zones
    # Since we don't have direct access to probe/forbidden info in the function signature,
    # we'll estimate them from the population and known constraints
    physics_prior = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Identify likely forbidden positions as those that appear infrequently or never in the population
    # Focus on positions that never appear (likely probe or forbidden) and rarely appear (likely forbidden)
    zero_count_positions = np.where(position_counts == 0)[0]
    rare_positions = np.where((position_counts > 0) & (position_counts < max(1, n_parents * 0.1)))[0]  # Increase threshold to 10%
    
    # Apply zero utility to positions that never appear (likely probe/forbidden)
    for pos in zero_count_positions:
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Apply zero utility to the position itself
        physics_prior[pos] = 0.0
        # Apply soft penalties to adjacent positions (Manhattan distance 1)
        for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
            for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
                    continue  # Skip the center position
                nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
                if 0 <= nr < grid_size and 0 <= nc < grid_size:
                    adj_idx = nr * grid_size + nc
                    # Reduce utility for adjacent positions
                    physics_prior[adj_idx] *= 0.3  # Stronger penalty than before
    
    # For rarely appearing positions, apply softer penalties
    for pos in rare_positions:
        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
        # Apply soft penalty to the position itself
        physics_prior[pos] *= 0.1  # Reduce utility significantly
        # Apply milder penalties to adjacent positions
        for dr in [-1, 0, 1]:
            for dc in [-1, 0, 1]:
                if dr == 0 and dc == 0:
                    continue  # Skip the center position
                nr, nc = row + dr, col + dc
                if 0 <= nr < grid_size and 0 <= nc < grid_size:
                    adj_idx = nr * grid_size + nc
                    # Reduce utility for adjacent positions but less severely
                    physics_prior[adj_idx] *= 0.7  # Milder penalty than for zero-count positions
    
    # For probe location estimation, find positions that are completely absent from the population
    # This is a better heuristic since probe locations would never appear in any valid solution
    # Boost utilities of positions close to zero-count positions (potential probe locations)
    for probe_pos in zero_count_positions:
        probe_row, probe_col = pos_to_coords[probe_pos]
        for pos_idx in range(grid_size * grid_size):
            row, col = pos_to_coords[pos_idx]
            # Manhattan distance to potential probe
            dist_to_probe = abs(row - probe_row) + abs(col - probe_col)
            if dist_to_probe > 0:
                # Higher utility for positions closer to potential probe (for high-frequency decoupling)
                # Use inverse relationship with some minimum value to avoid zero utility
                physics_prior[pos_idx] *= (1.0 + 0.8 / (dist_to_probe + 0.5))  # Increased influence
    
    # Combine occurrence-based utility with spatial importance, interaction scores and physics-aware prior
    total_uses = position_counts.sum()
    if total_uses > 0:
        occurrence_utilities = position_counts / total_uses
        # Weight the utilities by spatial importance, interaction scores and physics prior
        position_utilities = occurrence_utilities * spatial_importance * (1 + interaction_scores) * physics_prior
        # Normalize the combined utilities
        if position_utilities.sum() > 0:
            position_utilities = position_utilities / position_utilities.sum()
        else:
            position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    else:
        position_utilities = np.ones(grid_size * grid_size) / (grid_size * grid_size)
    
    # Set similarity thresholds for strategy selection based on empirical results
    low_similarity_threshold = 0.25  
    high_similarity_threshold = 0.55  
    
    # Generate offspring
    for i in range(n_pop):
        # Select two parents randomly
        parent_indices = np.random.choice(n_parents, 2, replace=False)
        parent1, parent2 = parents[parent_indices[0]], parents[parent_indices[1]]
        
        # Based on the similarity of parents, choose crossover strategy
        if avg_similarity < low_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are dissimilar - use uniform crossover for exploration
            # Use position utilities to bias inheritance toward higher utility positions
            mask = np.random.rand(n_decap) < 0.5
            child = np.where(mask, parent1, parent2)
            
            # Apply utility-based bias: with some probability, swap to the parent with higher utility at that position
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                # With some probability, pick the position with higher utility
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
                        
        elif avg_similarity > high_similarity_threshold:  # Parents are similar - use multi-point crossover to preserve good building blocks
            # Multi-point crossover with possibility of utility-based adjustments
            num_crossovers = np.random.choice([1, 2, 3], p=[0.5, 0.3, 0.2])  # Updated probabilities
            crossover_points = sorted(np.random.choice(range(1, n_decap), num_crossovers, replace=False))
            
            child = parent1.copy()
            current_parent = 0  # 0 for parent1, 1 for parent2
            
            prev_point = 0
            for cp in crossover_points:
                if current_parent == 0:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent1[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 1
                else:
                    child[prev_point:cp] = parent2[prev_point:cp]
                    current_parent = 0
                prev_point = cp
            
            # Fill remaining positions with the current parent
            if current_parent == 0:
                child[prev_point:] = parent1[prev_point:]
            else:
                child[prev_point:] = parent2[prev_point:]
                
            # Apply utility-based adjustments to the offspring
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.25:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        else:  # Default case: balanced approach with single-point crossover
            # Single-point crossover with utility-guided adjustments
            crossover_point = np.random.randint(1, n_decap)
            child = np.concatenate([parent1[:crossover_point], parent2[crossover_point:]])
            
            # Apply utility-based adjustments
            for idx in range(n_decap):
                pos1_utility = position_utilities[parent1[idx]]
                pos2_utility = position_utilities[parent2[idx]]
                
                if np.random.rand() < 0.2:  
                    if pos1_utility > pos2_utility:
                        child[idx] = parent1[idx]
                    else:
                        child[idx] = parent2[idx]
        
        # Duplicate resolution with spatial awareness
        unique_vals = set()
        duplicate_positions = []
        
        for idx, val in enumerate(child):
            if val in unique_vals:
                duplicate_positions.append(idx)
            else:
                unique_vals.add(val)
        
        if len(duplicate_positions) > 0:
            # Get available positions (not in current child)
            all_positions = set(range(grid_size * grid_size))
            available_positions = list(all_positions - unique_vals)
            
            if available_positions:  # If there are available positions
                for dup_idx in duplicate_positions:
                    # Get the coordinate of the position that needs replacement
                    original_pos = child[dup_idx]
                    orig_row, orig_col = pos_to_coords[original_pos]
                    
                    # Calculate Manhattan distances to all available positions
                    dists_and_pos = []
                    for pos in available_positions:
                        row, col = pos_to_coords[pos]
                        manhattan_dist = abs(orig_row - row) + abs(orig_col - col)
                        dists_and_pos.append((manhattan_dist, pos))
                    
                    # Sort by distance (prefer closer positions)
                    dists_and_pos.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
                    
                    # Select from top candidates (closest positions) and consider utilities
                    top_candidates = min(10, len(dists_and_pos))  # Use top 10 closest or all if fewer
                    candidate_positions = [item[1] for item in dists_and_pos[:top_candidates]]
                    
                    # Calculate weights based on both distance and utility
                    dist_weights = np.array([1/(i+1) for i in range(top_candidates)])  # Closer gets higher weight
                    utility_weights = np.array([position_utilities[pos] for pos in candidate_positions])  # Higher utility gets higher weight
                    
                    # Combine the weights
                    combined_weights = dist_weights * (utility_weights + 0.1)  # Add small constant to avoid zero utility
                    combined_weights /= combined_weights.sum()  # Normalize
                    
                    # Select based on combined weighted probabilities
                    selected_idx = np.random.choice(top_candidates, p=combined_weights)
                    selected_pos = dists_and_pos[selected_idx][1]
                    
                    # Update child and tracking sets
                    child[dup_idx] = selected_pos
                    unique_vals.add(selected_pos)
                    
                    # Remove selected position from available list
                    available_positions.remove(selected_pos)
        
        offspring[i] = child
    
    return offspring
